summary: Backend API completion for Supporter role — feedback, broadened read access, question search
description:
Closes the gap discovered while wiring the Phase 4 Supporter frontend (Weeks 7-8 role views) to the real backend. Verified against the live OpenAPI spec at /v3/api-docs, not just docs/api-reference.md — the feedback module and full-text question search were already spec'd in docs/backlog/phase-3-epic-weeks-7-8-feedback-job-search.json but were never actually implemented (no FeedbackResponse schema, no q param on GET /questions in the live spec). This epic scopes a focused completion of exactly what the Supporter frontend needs to function, rather than re-speccing that whole epic.

Also implements a new product decision made during this integration pass: supporters should not be scoped to only their own assigned processes/sessions the way candidates are scoped to their own process. Supporters should have the same breadth of READ access as marketer/admin across processes, sessions, clients, and questions. This does NOT extend to write actions — linking/unlinking questions and submitting feedback remain scoped to the assigned supporter, since those are data-integrity boundaries (a supporter must not be able to submit feedback or link questions under another supporter's name), not visibility restrictions.

Note for whoever picks up the feedback story: three sources currently disagree on the submit shape. The Phase 3 epic spec'd a separate `POST /sessions/:id/feedback/submit`; docs/api-reference.md documents `PATCH /sessions/:id/feedback` with `{ isSubmitted: true }`; the live backend has neither built. This epic specifies the PATCH approach (simpler, matches the currently-published docs) — reconcile docs/api-reference.md and the Phase 3 epic once built.

Key paths: <apps/api/src/main/java/com/ims/feedback>, <apps/api/src/main/java/com/ims/process>, <apps/api/src/main/java/com/ims/session>, <apps/api/src/main/java/com/ims/question>
functionality: read all processes/sessions/clients/questions, list sessions without knowing a process id in advance, search the question bank by text, and manage feedback for sessions they conducted
benefit: unblocks the already-built Phase 4 Supporter frontend (session list, question linking, feedback editor) and removes an unnecessary visibility restriction that doesn't match how supporters actually work across clients

stories.summary: Implement feedback draft, view, and submit lifecycle
stories.description:
Build the Feedback module: a supporter can create a draft, update it, and submit it (PATCH with isSubmitted: true), after which it is locked. Supporters can only read their own feedback; admins can read any submitted feedback for a session. This is the same scope as the unbuilt Phase 3 story (docs/backlog/phase-3-epic-weeks-7-8-feedback-job-search.json, "Implement feedback draft and submit lifecycle") but uses PATCH-based submit instead of a separate /submit endpoint, matching docs/api-reference.md.

Endpoints:
- GET /sessions/:id/feedback (supporter: own only; admin: any submitted) — 404 if no record exists
- POST /sessions/:id/feedback — creates a DRAFT record, { body }, supporterId from JWT, 409 if a record already exists
- PATCH /sessions/:id/feedback — { body?, isSubmitted? }, sets submittedAt server-side when isSubmitted flips to true, 409 on any further PATCH once submitted

Key paths: <apps/api/src/main/java/com/ims/feedback/FeedbackEntity.java>, <apps/api/src/main/java/com/ims/feedback/FeedbackService.java>, <apps/api/src/main/java/com/ims/feedback/FeedbackController.java>

acceptanceCriteria.when: no feedback record exists yet for the session
acceptanceCriteria.then: a feedback record is created with isSubmitted=false and a 201 response is returned

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Creating a second draft is rejected
acceptanceCriteria.given: a feedback record already exists for a session

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Draft can be updated before submission
acceptanceCriteria.then: the body is updated and updatedAt changes, isSubmitted remains false

acceptanceCriteria.when: PATCH /sessions/:id/feedback is called with { isSubmitted: true }
acceptanceCriteria.then: isSubmitted becomes true, submittedAt is set server-side, and a 200 response returns the updated record

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Submitted feedback cannot be edited further
acceptanceCriteria.when: PATCH /sessions/:id/feedback is called again with any field
acceptanceCriteria.then: a 409 Conflict response is returned and the record is unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Admin can read any submitted feedback for a session
acceptanceCriteria.given: a supporter has submitted feedback for a session
acceptanceCriteria.then: the submitted feedback record is returned

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Supporter cannot read another supporter's feedback
acceptanceCriteria.given: supporter A submitted feedback for a session originally assigned to supporter A
acceptanceCriteria.when: supporter B calls GET /sessions/:id/feedback for that session
acceptanceCriteria.then: a 403 Forbidden or 404 response is returned, not supporter A's feedback content

tasks.description: camelCase JSON fields per project convention: id, sessionId, supporterId, body, isSubmitted, submittedAt, updatedAt. No @JsonProperty snake_case annotations.

JPA entity mapping to the existing feedback table (already in the schema per docs/database-schema.md — no new migration expected unless the table is missing in the actual database). Service methods: createDraft, updateDraft, submit. Submit sets submitted_at and rejects further writes.

GET/POST/PATCH /sessions/:id/feedback. Enforce supporterId from JWT on create (cannot author feedback as another supporter). Supporter GET scoped to own record; admin GET unscoped to any submitted record for the session.

tasks.summary: Update docs/api-reference.md and cross-reference the Phase 3 epic
tasks.description: Confirm the PATCH-based submit shape is documented correctly. Add a note to docs/backlog/phase-3-epic-weeks-7-8-feedback-job-search.json's feedback story pointing at this epic as the one actually implemented, to avoid future confusion between the two specs.

stories.summary: Broaden supporter read access to processes and sessions; add unscoped session listing
stories.description:
Remove the 'own assigned sessions only' scoping for the supporter role on process and session read endpoints, matching marketer/admin visibility. Add supporter to the allowed roles on GET /processes (currently admin/marketer/candidate only). Add a new top-level GET /sessions endpoint — this both replaces the frontend's originally-assumed-but-nonexistent 'my sessions' endpoint and generalizes cleanly under the new broadened access model, since a supporter can still filter to their own sessions client-side or via a supporterId query param without needing a bespoke scoped route.

Write actions are explicitly NOT broadened by this story — POST/DELETE /sessions/:id/questions keep their existing 'must be the assigned supporter' constraint, and feedback stays self-authored via JWT (see the feedback story above). This story is read-access only.

Endpoints:
- GET /processes — add supporter to allowed roles, unscoped (same result set as marketer)
- GET /processes/:id/sessions — remove supporter 'own assigned only' scoping
- GET /sessions/:id — remove supporter 'own assigned only' scoping
- GET /sessions (new) — paginated, filterable by status/processId/supporterId, allowed for admin/marketer/supporter

Key paths: <apps/api/src/main/java/com/ims/process/ProcessController.java>, <apps/api/src/main/java/com/ims/session/SessionController.java>, <apps/api/src/main/java/com/ims/session/SessionService.java>

acceptanceCriteria.then: the full paginated process list is returned, same shape as when called by marketer, not filtered to processes containing the supporter's own sessions

stories.summary: Expose full-text question search via q parameter on GET /questions
stories.description:
The questions table already has a search_vector tsvector column and GIN index maintained by trigger (docs/database-schema.md) — this was built as part of the Phase 3 schema. What's missing is the API-layer q query parameter and search service, which is the remainder of the already-spec'd but unbuilt Phase 3 story (docs/backlog/phase-3-epic-weeks-7-8-feedback-job-search.json, "Implement full-text question search with PostgreSQL tsvector"). This story exists here scoped down to unblock the Supporter question-linking search box specifically; verify the migration/trigger is actually applied to the running database before assuming it's done.

Key paths: <apps/api/src/main/java/com/ims/question/QuestionSearchService.java>, <apps/api/src/main/java/com/ims/question/QuestionController.java>

acceptanceCriteria.then: only questions matching the search terms in body or topic are returned, ranked by relevance

acceptanceCriteria.then: existing clientId/topic-filtered, paginated behavior is unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Malformed search query does not crash the endpoint
acceptanceCriteria.given: a q parameter contains special characters that would break a raw tsquery
acceptanceCriteria.then: plainto_tsquery sanitises the input and a valid response is returned instead of a 500

Route to QuestionSearchService when q is present; keep existing behavior otherwise. Allowed roles unchanged (admin, marketer, supporter).
